subject: SIG: proposal for retrospective audit-event access and sample evidence
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finclear.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finclear.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — retrospective event access for investigations

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking through the SIG earlier. Two follow-ups from our security team: one on retention windows (policy vs. practical availability) and one on how FinClear can access or request event data for retrospective investigations. Specifically:

- What is Redwood's retention policy for control-plane and tenant event logs (audit events, token issuance, admin actions)?
- Can we request a time-bounded export for a specific tenant (e.g., a 48-hour window three months ago) for forensic analysis? If so: format, delivery mechanism, redaction policy, and SLA for delivery.
- Are there mechanisms for temporary, restricted access (read-only) to a filtered event stream for a customer investigator? If yes, what controls and auditing exist around that access?

We also need example evidence to attach to our SIG request: a sample audit extract (redacted) and the SIG mapping you completed. Could you provide those or point us to the artifacts and steps for requesting retrospective access?

Appreciate a short plan and an approximate delivery timeline.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Security Engineer — FinClear
security@finclear.com

--
Attachment: initial-sig-questions.pdf (stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finclear.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — retrospective event access for investigations

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary and proposed approach below; I'm looping in Marissa (Audit/evidence) and Rishi (Customer reliability) to confirm operational steps.

Summary / short answers:
- Retention policy: control-plane logs are retained 13 months for SLA-backed accounts; tenant-level event streams (application inference requests) are kept 90 days by default for hosted accounts, configurable in Dedicated/Private.
- Time-bounded exports: Yes — we can produce a redacted CSV export for a specified tenant/time window. We deliver via a pre-signed S3 URL (7-day expiry) or secure SFTP depending on your procurement needs. Typical turnaround: 3 business days for windows within retention, 7-10 days if we need to rehydrate from longer-term archives.
- Temporary access: We can provision a scoped, read-only IAM role with access to a filtered event bucket for up to 72 hours. All role assumptions are logged and we provide an access audit report as part of the handoff.

Proposed immediate deliverables for your SIG packet:
1) Completed SIG mapping XLSX (attached) — answers to the audit log questions and references to evidence IDs.
2) One redacted sample export showing schema and redaction approach (attached).
3) A runbook excerpt describing the export request flow and SLAs.

Operational notes for Marissa / Rishi:
- If the customer requests a retrospective window older than tenant retention, confirm whether logs are in cold archive and estimate rehydration work.
- We need to verify redaction rules: IP address hashing vs full removal as per FinClear policy.
- Who signs off on temporary IAM roles for third-party investigators? Provide approval chain.

Lena — if this plan works I'll push the sample artifacts and next steps today.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — retrospective event access for investigations

Kim / Rishi — confirming operational steps and adding a couple of clarifications:

1) Export flow: submit a Support ticket referencing the FinClear HubSpot ID and the requested window (UTC). We will stage an export job that creates a CSV with the standard event schema and applies redaction rules. Default TTL for pre-signed URLs is 7 days; we can extend on request with justification.

2) Redaction: By default we pseudonymize IPs (sha256) and remove values for any PII fields. If the customer requires different handling (e.g., tokenized IDs), that must be documented in a data processing amendment.

3) Temp access: we can create a scoped role with read-only access to a dedicated export bucket. Approval steps: Security Manager -> Product Ops -> Customer Success lead. Estimated time to provision: ~4 business hours once approvals complete.

4) Evidence artifacts: I've uploaded the two files Kim attached to the shared SIG folder and added a runbook excerpt: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/SIG/FinClear/2026/ (link below). I created ticket INF-7421 to track the customer's export request if they proceed.

Marissa Cole
